did_you_know.text: Did you know? 2 Samuel 23 opens with honorific titles for David: he is presented as the son of Jesse, the one appointed by the Lord, and the “sweet psalmist of Israel.”
Did you know? David testifies that the “Spirit of the Lord” spoke through him and that God’s word was on his tongue, describing his words as divinely inspired.
Did you know? David presents a principle of good leadership: the one who rules over people must be righteous and fear God.
Did you know? Righteous rule is compared in this chapter to the light of a clear morning and to rain that makes grass grow—images of blessing, stability, and renewal.

Did you know? David connects his hope to an everlasting covenant with the Lord, described as ordered and secure. By contrast, worthless men are compared to thorns that are thrown away and cannot be picked up by hand.

Did you know? The list of David’s mighty warriors begins with Josheb-basshebeth son of Hachmoni, also called Adino the Eznite and chief of the three; according to the text, he struck down eight hundred men at one time.
Did you know? Eleazar son of Dodo, one of the Ahohites, fought the Philistines until his hand clung to his sword—a description emphasizing his endurance in battle.
Did you know? Shammah son of Agee fought alone to defend a field full of lentils after the people fled from the Philistines; here too, the Lord’s deliverance is emphasized.

Did you know? Three of David’s mighty warriors broke through the Philistine camp and drew water for him from the well at Bethlehem. David did not drink it, but poured it out to the Lord because he regarded it as the blood of the men who had risked their lives.

Did you know? Benaiah son of Jehoiada was known for three separate acts of heroism: he struck down two champions of Moab, went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion, and later struck down an Egyptian with the Egyptian’s own weapon.
Did you know? Benaiah was honored above the thirty warriors, but he did not attain the rank of the first three; David appointed him over his bodyguard.
Did you know? The list ends with Uriah the Hittite and totals thirty-seven warriors, although the chapter also mentions different ranks within the group of mighty warriors.
